principles.statement: For TSP variant problem #44 with N up to 200K and 2-second time limit, grid-based nearest-neighbor construction accounts for ~93% of the final score (64.5 out of 69.5). SA optimization with random swap + 2-opt adds only ~5 points.
principles.regime: N up to 200K, 2-second time limit, cities sorted by x-coordinate
principles.mechanism: For N=200K, random SA evaluates O(10M) moves in 1.7s. With O(N^2) = 4*10^10 possible swap pairs, coverage is <0.1%. Most random moves don't improve the tour. Construction quality determines the starting point, and SA can only make local refinements.
principles.applicability_bounds: Applies when N is large (>10K) and time limit is tight (2s). For small N (<1000), SA has much better coverage and construction matters less.

principles.statement: The penalty structure (10% surcharge on every 10th step when source is non-prime) contributes at most ~1% to total tour cost. Prime scheduling post-pass captures most available savings but adds <1 point to score.
principles.regime: N up to 200K with ~18K primes and ~N/10 penalty positions
principles.mechanism: With N/10 penalty positions and 10% surcharge per position, max penalty contribution is 10% * 10% = 1% of tour cost. Primes cover ~90% of penalty positions at max N, leaving limited room for optimization.
principles.applicability_bounds: Specific to this problem's penalty structure. Different penalty rates or prime densities would change the calculus.

principles.statement: 2-opt with boundary-only delta approximation (ignoring internal penalty changes from segment reversal) provides comparable optimization to exact range recompute, while enabling ~10x more iterations per second.
principles.regime: TSP with sparse step-based penalties, segment lengths 2-200
principles.mechanism: Boundary-only delta is O(1) per evaluation vs O(segment_length) for exact recompute. Since penalties affect only 10% of steps, the approximation error is small. Periodic full recompute corrects drift.
principles.applicability_bounds: Works when penalties are sparse (every 10th step). Would fail for dense penalty structures.
